decision: Does TensorLBM's fill-gradient interface normal (src/tensorlbm/free_surface_lbm.py:642 _compute_interface_normal: fill=mass/rho, central difference, normalized, sign liquid->gas) reproduce the mature OSS practice (Maarten-vd-Sande/lbm, oss_solutions id=85 'fill-gradient-normal': n=0.5*(eps_{i-1}-eps_{i+1}, eps_{j-1}-eps_{j+1}), NOT normalized, sign liquid->gas) within the owner 15% criterion, and which knobs (normalization, eps gas value, dimensionality) carry the difference?

alternatives.A1_tensorlbm: TensorLBM as-is: fill=mass/rho, central difference via roll, normalized to unit, n=-grad/|grad| (liquid->gas)
alternatives.A2_oss_clean: OSS as documented (oss id=85): n=0.5*(eps_{i-1}-eps_{i+1}, eps_{j-1}-eps_{j+1}), unnormalized, eps in {0,1} (GAS=0, FLUID=1)
alternatives.A3_oss_bug: OSS with the documented streamcollide.py:166 priority bug: GAS returns eps=0.5 -> magnitude underest 2x, sign unchanged
alternatives.A4_analytic: Analytic normal of the constructed interface (circle: radial; plane: constant; sphere: radial) = ground truth

hypothesis: H1: direction agreement between A1 and A2 (and vs A4) stays below the 15% criterion at all resolutions, i.e. the central-difference fill-gradient stencil is the shared core and only normalization/eps-convention differ; H0 (falsifier): 1-mean|cos(theta)| >= 0.15 on any geometry at the finest resolution.

metrics.dir_err_vs_analytic: 1 - mean(|n_computed . n_analytic|) over interface cells (0=perfect, 1=orthogonal); reported per arm per geometry
metrics.angle_deg_vs_analytic: mean angle (deg) between computed and analytic normal over interface cells
metrics.dir_err_a1_vs_a2: 1 - mean(|n_A1 . n_A2|) over cells where both are nonzero (cross-implementation)
metrics.mag_ratio: mean(|n_A2|)/mean(|n_A1|) over interface cells (expected ~0.5 for sharp axis-aligned, geometry-dependent otherwise)

unit_of_analysis: one (geometry, resolution) cell-set; KPIs are scalars per arm

baseline_control.control: A2/A3 share the identical stencil and fill field with A1; only normalization (A1 vs A2) and eps gas value (A2 vs A3) differ, isolating each knob
baseline_control.cross_implementation_note: OSS arms are formula transplants evaluated on the identical fill field (zero hand-copy: formula taken verbatim from oss_solutions id=85 method field); a full OSS code run was not possible in this environment (no network checkout) - see friction log

predeclared_thresholds.interpretation: dir_err (1-mean|cos|) must be < 0.15 for A1 vs A4 and A1 vs A2 on every geometry at the finest resolution for H1 to hold
predeclared_thresholds.convergence_rule: report dir_err at N in {64,128,256} for the circle; a KPI is resolution-converged when |KPI(256)-KPI(128)|/KPI(256) < 10%; otherwise the N=128 value is reported as resolution-limited
predeclared_thresholds.interface_cell_rule: cells with 0 < eps < 1 in the constructed fill field, or (for sharp 0/1 fields) cells with a nonzero computed normal and |n|_A1 > 1e-6
predeclared_thresholds.stability_rule: a cell-set with fewer than 20 interface cells is excluded and reported, not tuned

stopping_rule: fixed geometry set {circle 2D, tilted plane 2D, sphere 3D} and fixed resolution ladder {64,128,256} (3D sphere at {32,64,128}); no arm extended after inspecting KPIs. Wall-clock budget: 600 s total (pure numpy/torch CPU, no cluster needed).
variables_changed: eps gas value 0 vs 0.5 (A2 vs A3)
variables_controlled: fill field construction (same eps for all arms)
periodic roll boundary (as in both source implementations)
confounders: staircase discretization of curved interfaces (mitigated by resolution ladder)
periodic wrap-around at domain edges (mitigated: interface kept >= 2 cells from domain boundary)

sharp vs smeared fill: TensorLBM production fill is mass/rho (can be smeared); here both arms receive the same sharp field so the stencil comparison is isolated; smearing sensitivity reported as a separate sensitivity point
analysis: aggregation = mean over interface cells; uncertainty = std/sqrt(n_cells); no outlier removal (all interface cells kept); comparison = direct vector dot, no fitting
safety_resource_limits: CPU only, < 2 GB RAM, < 600 s wall clock; no cluster submission needed
